description:
The redo record reaches disk synced, with its directory fsynced, before a mutation performs its first live write.

## Background

A redo-only commit protocol has no rollback: once the first live file is replaced there is no way back, so the record is already durable at that moment. The shared atomic-write helper writes a temp file and renames it, with no `sync_all` on the file and no fsync on the parent directory, so it gives reader-visibility atomicity. The one synced write primitive in the tree is the transaction kernel's staging helper, which is retiring.

The helper therefore gains the two operations the record needs: a synced file write and a directory fsync.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Writing a redo record returns after the record's bytes are synced to disk and its containing directory is fsynced.
- [hard] REQ-02: The shared atomic-write module exposes a synced write and a directory fsync as named operations, reached by every caller that needs either.
- [hard] REQ-03: The scratch directory is created when absent, with a mode matching the rest of the data root.
- [hard] REQ-04: A record write that fails partway leaves a residue a later session skips rather than replays.
- [hard] REQ-05: Durability behaviour is covered at the storage unit layer without a wall-clock assertion.

## Notes

Expected additive footprint is under 120 production lines across the record writer and the atomic-write module. Per-file replacement during replay stays on the existing temp-file-and-rename path, whose crash survivability rests on the record.
title: Durable redo record write
